docs.title: Stoway
docs.text:
A Roblox inventory framework built in layers, one branch per layer. The core is a pure-Luau inventory engine (CoreStore) — no Roblox types, no UI, no networking — inside server orchestration, inside a Fusion client.

flowchart LR
    UI[Client UI<br/>StowayClientV3] --> NET[Network<br/>QuickNet routes]
    NET --> SV[Server<br/>StowayServerV3_0_0]
    SV --> CORE[CoreStore<br/>pure Luau]
    SV --> PUSH[pushes back<br/>deltas + FullSync]
    PUSH --> UI

CoreStore owns the inventory truth. Everything else reads from it or writes to it through its public API.

New here? Quickstart → Life of a swap → Building on top.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
registerAdapter is the real server seam. Every route result — success or failure, client-originated or not — is dispatched to every registered adapter as { operation, replicate, result }. Communications (the QuickNet bridge) is just one adapter.

A 15-line adapter that logs every failure:

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Services = game:GetService("ServerScriptService"):WaitForChild("Services")
local Stoway = require(Services:WaitForChild("StowayServerV3_0_0"))

Stoway.registerAdapter(function(player, signal)
    if not signal.result.ok then
        warn(("[Audit] %s failed for %s: %s"):format(
            signal.operation,
            player.Name,
            signal.result.error.message
        ))
    end
end)

The same seam drives persistence (save on removePlayer's returned state), analytics, or admin tooling — without touching routes. See Persistence.

Adapters that call routes must defer

Dispatch runs inside the route while it still holds the per-player lock, so a nested route call fails with OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS. Wrap follow-up writes in task.defer — the lock is free by then.

docs.title: CoreStore runs twice
docs.text:
The same CoreStore module lives in ReplicatedStorage, so it runs on the server (to decide) and on the client (to predict). When you drag, your client applies the move instantly using the same rules, then asks the server. Agree: nothing more is sent. Disagree: the server pushes a FullSync and your client snaps back. That is why CoreStore has no Roblox types — and why a stale structural setting (MaxHotbarSlots, CanStack…) forks state.

Dependency direction (client → server → CoreStore) is about authority, not imports: the client also runs the shared CoreStore itself. CoreStore never imports upward.

Disk maps to Roblox services via default.project.json: ReplicatedStorage → ReplicatedStorage, src/server → ServerScriptService, src/client → StarterPlayerScripts. GUI prefabs and Tool templates live in the .rbxl only (see Skins & Layouts).

docs.title: InventoryState
docs.text:
{
  Items: { [uuid] = Item },            -- O(1): UUID → Item
  ItemsByID: { [id] = { uuid } },      -- O(1): ItemId → UUIDs
  Hotbar: { [slot] = uuid? },          -- 1..MaxHotbarSlots, Static has holes
  Storage: { uuid, ... },              -- packed array, no holes
  LocationByUUID: { [uuid] = SlotRef },-- O(1): UUID → where
  MetadataIndex: { field → value → { uuid } }, -- indexed: Rarity, Type
  EquippedItemUUID: uuid?,
  Weight: number,                      -- sum of Amounts
  Settings: Settings,
}
-- Item = { UUID, Id, Amount, Metadata }

docs.title: Operation lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Route call] --> B[route: per-player lock]
    B --> C[CoreStore mutation]
    C --> D[dispatch to adapters]
    D --> E{replicate?}
    E -->|yes| F[push delta or FullSync]
    E -->|no| G[done, client already optimistic]
    F --> H[client applies + converges]
  • Server: every route runs under a per-player lock (3s timeout returns OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS). replicate is opt-in — omitted means no echo.
  • Client: drags apply optimistically, then one FireServer per op. Server rejects arrive as revert + FullSync; reverts are log-only, never re-requested.
  • Settings: designer defaults seed each state; changes push sparsely (SettingsChanged) with FullSync as backstop. The client overlays pushed settings onto its mirror state first, then fans out to atoms.

docs.title: Building on Top
docs.text: Stoway is a base system. Features plug in at three seams without touching the engine: a metadata key, a server gate or stamp, and a client read. Every shipped example follows this recipe.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
1. Server owns truth. Only the server writes authoritative state. The client predicts for feel, then converges on pushes. React to results through registerAdapter — Communications is just one adapter.
  2. Metadata is the extension API. New behavior = new keys on items, not new engine branches. Stacking identity, visual contracts, and showcase features all ride on metadata (see Metadata).
  3. Replicate deliberately. replicate defaults off. Push deltas for single-item changes, FullSync when many things moved or a client must converge wholesale.
  4. Never write atoms directly. Pushed state funnels through the mirror (ApplyServer*), then one sync() fans out. Direct atom writes get clobbered by the next op.

docs.title: The feature recipe
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Pick a metadata key] --> B[Server: gate or stamp it on a route]
    B --> C[Client: read it for feedback]
    C --> D[Converge via push or FullSync]

Worked example (cooldowns): designer sets Cooldown + FireOnEquip; the EquipSlot route stamps CooldownEnd and refuses locked equips; the client veils cooling slots from the same key; FullSync delivers stamps fired elsewhere. Zero changes to Operations/Slots.

docs.title: The StowayPickup pattern
docs.text: World drops are the template for server-owned glue: Drop tags a live Tool (Stoway tag, touch stripped, 5 studs ahead); StowayPickup.server.luau watches the tag, attaches a ProximityPrompt, and on trigger reads attributes back into AddToBackpack — destroying the tool on success. One watcher, weak keys, no per-tool scripts.

docs.title: Pitfalls that bite feature authors
docs.text:
• Writing Fusion atoms directly instead of the mirror state.
  • Reading a live Instance property as a Computed fallback (self-perpetuating).
  • scope:ForPairs with side effects but no Observer (lazy For never runs).
  • Sync once per mutation; a second sync re-runs every dependent Computed.
  • { Key = nil } deletes nothing — use CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE.
  • Move never stacks; StackOnSwap is swap-only. Design merges accordingly.

docs.title: Production Builds
docs.text: Non-production ships as-is: debug console, test harnesses, op-signal bus. Production strips them. What you get is the example without the test suite — then you build your own commands or your own tests on the seams below.

Keep Libraries/PlayerServiceSignals — that is the production player-lifecycle bus, not test machinery.

docs.text:
• Chat commands: the Debug/ folder shape is the template — one module, RegisterAll(stoway), one call in Server.server.luau. Ship yours, or ship none and drive everything through routes.
  • Tests: the Tests/ observers are the template — subscribe, peek, print, delete before committing.

docs.title: Client Events & Hooks
docs.text: The UI bus (ClientEvents) plus the Store atoms plus SetLayout are the whole client surface feature code should touch.

docs.title: The bus
docs.text: SlotClicked, SlotHovered, DragStarted, DragEnded, Equipped, Unequipped, ItemAdded, ItemRemoved, Swapped, Selected, Deselected. Subscribe, never emit (layouts own emission).

docs.title: The atoms
docs.text: ClientStore.Items / Hotbar / Storage / EquippedItemUUID / Weight / Settings — read with Fusion.peek, derive with Computed. Never write them; sync() owns that.

docs.title: Layouts and hooks
docs.text: LayoutManager.SetLayout(scope, playerGui, store, hotbarType, skin) mounts live. Skins expose Hooks (HookFuncs/ in the prefab); layouts invoke them via ClientEvents.CallHook (spawned + pcall'd, so a throwing hook warns once and never breaks inventory).

docs.title: Cookbook
docs.text:
Toast on ItemAdded, sound on Equipped:

ClientEvents.ItemAdded:Connect(function(slotType, slot)
    Toast.show(("Picked up something in %s %d"):format(slotType, slot))
end)

ClientEvents.Equipped:Connect(function()
    SoundService:PlayLocalSound(equipSound)
end)

A custom skin hook (in the prefab's HookFuncs module):

return {
    OnEquip = function(slotType, slot)
        -- flash the frame, play a tween, notify quests
    end,
}

docs.title: Debug Console
docs.text:
Conch debug console, Studio only (Backquote to toggle). Client and server halves mount gated on RunService:IsStudio() — production gets no remotes, no role, no commands.

All commands act on the calling player and replicate. Item ids are exact-match names of templates in ServerStorage.Tools. UUIDs contain a . from os.clock(), and the console language truncates an unquoted token at that dot, so quote every UUID (remove "core-..."). inv prints UUIDs pre-quoted for copy-paste; prefer slot commands such as equip-slot <Hotbar|Storage> <slot> where one exists. There is no toggle for BackpackEnabled, so addback fails with BACKPACK_DISABLED once a settings change turns storage off (storage is on by default).

Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. message is the reason string; kind tells you the class.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
CoreStore: pure-Luau engine. No Roblox types, no UI, no networking.

Route: a server function (SwapSlots, Drop…) that locks, mutates, and dispatches to adapters.

Adapter: a function registered with registerAdapter that reacts to every route result. Communications (the QuickNet bridge) is one; a logger or a saver would be others.

Replicate: opt-in flag that echoes a server-side change to the client. Omitted means silent.

FullSync: whole-inventory push — items, slots, equipped, weight, and the settings snapshot. Heals any divergence wholesale.

Optimistic: the client applies first, the server corrects.

Layout: the engine that decides behavior (HotbarType). Skin: the look. A layout mounts against a skin at boot.

Atom: a Fusion Value in ClientStore (Items, Hotbar, Storage, EquippedItemUUID, Weight, Settings).

Hotbar / Storage / Backpack: Hotbar is the slot row; Storage is the packed array; "Backpack" is the UI name for Storage.

SlotRef: { Type: "Hotbar"|"Storage", Slot: number } — every slot address in the system.

docs.title: Life of a swap
docs.text:
After this page you can trace any operation end to end, success and failure.

You drag the sword from slot 1 to slot 3. Here is everything that happens.

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Player
    participant C as Client (CoreStore copy)
    participant N as QuickNet
    participant S as Server route
    participant K as Server CoreStore
    P->>C: drag slot 1 to slot 3
    C->>C: CoreStore.swap, atoms update, UI moves
    C->>N: SwapSlots { from, to }
    N->>S: Communications listener
    S->>K: lock, CoreStore.swap
    alt accepted
        K-->>S: ok (replicate = false)
        S-->>C: nothing. Silence means agreement.
    else rejected
        K-->>S: error
        S-->>C: InventoryRevert (log-only) + FullSync
        C->>C: replace state wholesale, UI snaps back
    end
  1. Predict. The client runs the swap on its own copy of CoreStore.
  2. Ask. One FireServer per op.
  3. Decide. The route takes a per-player lock, runs the real swap, and dispatches to adapters.
  4. Stay quiet or correct. Client-originated ops do not echo on success. Failures correct through FullSync.

Server-initiated changes are the opposite

Console commands and game code call routes with replicate = true, which pushes deltas (add, remove, equip) or a FullSync (swap, move, split, metadata, sort) so the client learns about changes it did not predict.

Next: Building on top.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Metadata is the whole game. Four systems read the same open { [string]: MetadataValue? } dict: the index (O(1) find), stacking identity (required fields), visual contracts (rarity/type/team/image), and showcase features (cooldowns, locks, glow). Learn the dict and you can extend Stoway without touching the engine.

docs.title: Canon keys
docs.text:
Key Type Read by Rarity string Stacking blacklist + required field, rarity sort (descending), rarity frame tint, O(1) index Type string Required field, storage section key, O(1) index Image string Slot button image (empty → Id fallback text) Description string Storage search only Droppable boolean Drop route (false → NOT_DROPPABLE), defaults from DefaultDroppable (true when unset) IsGamepass boolean Reserved open key Team string Slot ring + keybind tint (Colors.getTeamColor); set-team stamps it Id / Amount top-level Fallback label / stack badge (not metadata)

Plus two engine-level rules: updateMetadata merges keys and never re-stacks; deleting a key needs the CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE sentinel ({ Key = nil } is an empty table, not a deletion).

docs.title: Showcase keys (example branches)
docs.text:
Keys Idea Cooldown + FireOnEquip / server-stamped CooldownEnd Cooldowns: skills on metadata UnlocksHotbarSlot + Settings.LockedHotbarSlots Locked Slots: consume-to-unlock IsNew (client-ephemera, server strips silently) New-Item Glow: first-seen shine

Each works because the engine treats unknown keys as inert payload: features add gates, stamps, and reads around Operations, never inside it.

docs.title: Wire note
docs.text: Metadata crosses the wire as an open string map. Canon does not filter it: client AddItem / AddToBackpack / AddToHotbar / UpdateMetadata payloads reach the routes unfiltered — see the trust model before relying on any metadata-driven rule. FullSync carries full metadata, so anything the server stamps eventually converges everywhere.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
State is per session; nothing saves. createPlayer builds it, removePlayer returns it — those two are your hook points.

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    local state = Stoway.removePlayer(player)
    if state then
        MySaver.save(player.UserId, state.Items, state.Hotbar, state.Storage)
    end
end)

Save items, slots, and backpack-relevant metadata; rebuild with createPlayer(player, overrides) + AddItem on next join. Decide what EquippedItemUUID, Weight, and volatile keys (cooldown ends, IsNew glows) mean across sessions — usually: drop them.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Ten minutes, three commands

Install tools → open the place → press Play.

After this page you can run the inventory and poke it from the console.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Roblox Studio with the Rojo plugin
  • Rokit, then rokit install in the repo (installs Rojo, Wally, and luau-lsp from rokit.toml)

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
1. Open stoway.rbxl. Skin prefabs and Tool templates live in the place file, not the repo, so a bare rojo build has no GUI.
  2. rojo serve, then Connect in the Rojo plugin.
  3. Press Play (solo).
  4. Press ++backquote++ to open the Conch console, then try help and inv.

docs.title: What you will actually see
docs.text:
Players get their defaults from Shared/Stoway/Settings.luau, not the engine:

Setting You get Engine default Layout / skin StandardHotbarStorage / Default n/a HotbarType Dynamic Static CanStack false true BackpackEnabled true true

So: a hotbar row plus the storage toggle, no merging into existing stacks. A single add still creates stacks up to MaxStackSize. To try the bare engine defaults instead, run set-hotbar-type Static; to explore the code-built skins, run set-skin Jailbreak or set-skin Persona (both switch to JailbreakHotbar).

addhot Pickaxe 1 3

docs.title: Roadmap & Known Limitations
docs.text:
Near-term, in rough order:

  • Persistence. State is per session; the createPlayer / removePlayer hook points exist, no saver ships.
  • Client Add*/UpdateMetadata policy. The trust model calls this out: client-originated item/mutation payloads reach routes unfiltered.
  • Failure-correction rate limits. Only sync requests are throttled.
  • Moonwave API extraction. The facade reference is hand-maintained; revisit when it hurts.

Next: Glossary.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Engine settings steer behavior; the client mirrors them into atoms. Two default sets exist — know which one players get.

docs.title: The two defaults
docs.text: Players get Shared/Stoway/Settings.luau (Dynamic hotbar, merging off, backpack on, Default skin on StandardHotbarStorage). CoreStore/State.luau holds engine fallbacks (Static, merging on, backpack on). createPlayer maps the shared set onto the engine explicitly (defaultOverrides); explicit caller overrides win.

docs.title: Every setting
docs.text:
Setting What it does Kind HotbarType Static keeps fixed slots (holes allowed); Dynamic packs and auto-compacts. Structural MaxHotbarSlots Number of hotbar slots (1..N). Structural Limit Total Amount capacity. 0 = unlimited. Structural-lite CanStack Allows merging into existing stacks. Does not cap new stacks. Structural MaxStackSize Max Amount per stack. Caps new stacks and splits; existing stacks are not re-split. Structural BackpackEnabled Allows Storage. false rejects storage operations. Structural-lite StackOnSwap Allows swap/swapStack to merge. Requires CanStack; move and split never merge. Structural StackRequiredFields Metadata fields that must match before merging. Structural StackBlacklist Rarity values that never merge into existing stacks. Structural DefaultDroppable Droppable default for new items that omit it. Structural-lite Sorting Auto-sorts Storage after every mutation. Hotbar is never sorted. Cosmetic SortOrder Sort key: None, Name, Rarity (descending), or ItemType. Cosmetic DebugLogs System print/warn output. Console and hooks use their own paths. Cosmetic

Structural settings must match on both copies or client prediction diverges from server decisions. Structural-lite fields affect capacity, gating, or new-item defaults. Cosmetic fields only misrender until the next update.

Stacking trap: CanStack = false blocks merges into existing stacks. It is not MaxStackSize = 1 — a single add still creates stacks up to MaxStackSize, so add apple 5 with the default cap produces one stack of 5. Set MaxStackSize = 1 when you want one item per unit.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text: Changes push sparsely as SettingsChanged patches; every FullSync carries the full snapshot as backstop. The client overlays patches onto its mirror state first, then fans out — never writes atoms directly.

docs.title: How to add a setting
docs.text: Touch all of these or it silently won't replicate: the Settings and SettingsOverrides type blocks, the FullSyncPayload.Settings shape, both default tables, defaultOverrides, the FullSync projection, the SettingsChanged and FullSync wire schemas, the client get/set pair, and ApplyServerSettings.

docs.title: Skins & Layouts
docs.text: The client splits behavior from look: HotbarType picks a layout engine, UiSkin picks a skin loader. LayoutManager mounts one against the other, so new presentations land without touching state, controller, or slots.

docs.title: Mount flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Settings.Layout + UiSkin] --> B[LayoutManager.SetLayout]
    B --> C[Teardown previous scope]
    C --> D[Skin loader builds GUI]
    D --> E[Engine mounts views + input]
    E --> F[Swaps only re-mount]

SetLayout looks up the engine and loader (warns on unknown keys), tears down the old scope, loads the skin prefab, and mounts. A server LayoutChanged push re-mounts live.

docs.title: The engines
docs.text:
Engine Shape StandardHotbarStorage Static holes / Dynamic packed hotbar 1..Max, sectioned storage by Type with collapse + search + weight, full IAS input (PC/console/touch), ghost drag JailbreakHotbar Circular bottom hotbar + centered popup, sweep paint-to-move, swap-pop tween, lean binds

Both call into Layouts/Shared: getMaxSlots, isBackpackEnabled, hasDestItem (drives Swap-vs-Move), handleSwap/handleMove (warn-on-reject), doEquipSlot (Dynamic visible→packed mapping, empty slot unequips), ensureDraggingGui (adopt-or-create the drag ghost), and bindResponsiveUi (code-built skins: popup above the hotbar, mobile toggle above the left slots).

docs.title: The skin contract
docs.text:
Prefab skins live in the .rbxl at ReplicatedStorage/Stoway/GUI/<SkinName>/ — flat, exactly one ScreenGui plus Slot/, never in the repo. The loader clones it into PlayerGui and returns a handle: Gui, HotbarFrame, BackpackFrame, ScrollingFrame, WeightLabel, SearchFilter, BackpackStuff, slot template (slotbutton, stackcount, slotnumber, selecticon, rarityframe), DraggingGui. Optional Slot-folder attributes tune hiding (GhostHidden / HideInStorage / HideInHotbar, comma-separated) and bleed (SlotBleedPx).

Three optional handle fields let a skin take over chrome the generic views would otherwise own — all nil-safe, so prefab skins are unaffected:

Field Lets a skin HeaderColors Tint storage category headers per category key HeaderStyle Replace the whole header look (fill, transparency, text color/size, FontFace, corner, UIStroke color/thickness/line join, left/right padding) ResponsiveUi Opt into layout-owned popup + mobile toggle geometry (see below); PopupTopOverhang reserves skin art that hangs over the popup's top edge

Two skins are code-built instead of prefabs — same handle shape, no .rbxl asset, GUI built in Lua by the skin module:

Skin Layout Notes Jailbreak JailbreakHotbar Circular dark slots, no hooks table Persona JailbreakHotbar Slanted ink cards + red shard, ships its own hooks table

docs.title: The Persona skin
docs.text:
Skins/Persona is the slanted-ink skin: every card, tag and shard leans -6 degrees, white miter outlines, ink fill, one red accent (235,35,55) — the same language as the combo counter. The look lives in Persona/Theme.luau (palette, font, tilt, card geometry), so a tweak lands once.

It ships its own hook table (Persona/Hooks.luau), so the visuals ride the skin hooks without a HookFuncs prefab folder: all eleven hooks are wired to a punch in Persona/Fx.luau (elastic kick, white flash, edge flicker, slash burst, shockwave ring, equipped-bar pulse). Persona/Fx.luau is plain TweenService — no per-frame loop, no Fusion objects per event — and every effect is parented to the skin's full-screen Fx overlay so the storage grid can't clip it.

The drag marker belongs to the destination, not the source: the sweep arms on the pressed card (OnDragStart), but OnSlotHover moves the hot outline (Fx:SetHot) to the slot under the pointer, and OnDragEnd drops it. Only one card is ever lit.

Switch it with set-skin Persona (it pairs itself with the JailbreakHotbar layout).

docs.title: Responsive geometry
docs.text:
Prefab skins carry authored Backpack / BackpackStuff positions: the layout leaves them alone. Code-built skins have no prefab to author, so they set SkinHandle.ResponsiveUi = true and Shared.bindResponsiveUi owns the two pieces that break on small screens:

  • Popup — bottom-anchored, centered over the hotbar with a 12px gap. Its height is clamped to the space between the safe area's top and the hotbar (minus PopupTopOverhang), its width to the safe-area width. It can never cover a slot, in Static or Dynamic.
  • Mobile toggle — sits above the left end of the hotbar (so it clears Roblox's jump button and the centered popup), 8px above the slots. Its size follows the live slot size (0.8x, clamped 32–44px) instead of a fixed 48/44px, so the glyph scales with the bar.

Geometry is read from the live safe-area + hotbar rectangles, not camera math, so rotation and device resize re-flow without a remount. The tracking tick is deferred and coalesced: AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize also change during a Fusion graph change (the hotbar resizing itself), and setting a Value from inside a graph change trips Fusion's infinite-loop guard.

Both Jailbreak and Persona opt in. StandardHotbarStorage also skips its own bottom-reserve Size binding for these skins, since the popup geometry is already clamped.

docs.title: Authoring checklist
docs.text:
• A new skin: one ScreenGui + Slot/template with the named nodes, then a thin loader stamping look data. Missing nodes are nil-safe; views skip them.
  • A new code-built skin (Jailbreak, Persona): a module that builds the GUI in Lua and returns the same handle — no prefab, no .rbxl asset.
  • A new layout: one Mount(scope, skin, store) using Shared for commits and SlotView.Create per slot; register it in LayoutManager.
  • Slot chrome (image, stack badge, rarity, team ring, keybind, equip) is shared in SlotView — layouts don't reimplement it.

docs.title: Tools & Templates
docs.text: Items are data; Tools are what the character holds. Templates bridge them.

docs.title: The ServerStorage.Tools contract
docs.text:
• Template name = item Id (exact match). No template → AddItem fails with ITEM_NOT_IN_TOOLS_FOLDER.
  • Template attributes become metadata defaults: Description (""), Image (""), Droppable (true; or the player's DefaultDroppable when the attribute is absent), IsGamepass (false), Rarity ("Common"), Type ("Material"). Caller metadata wins on conflict.
  • Equipped clones get UUID, Amount, Id, plus every metadata key stamped as attributes.

docs.title: Equip, unequip, drop
docs.text:
• Equip clears stale character Tools, clones the template, removes the reserved world-drop tag, and parents to the Character (which equips it).
  • Unequip clears character Tools.
  • Drop reuses the equipped tool when dropping the whole stack, else clones; syncs the Amount attribute; touch-strips the handle, pivots 5 studs ahead, parents to Workspace, and tags it Stoway — which is what StowayPickup watches for (ProximityPrompt → AddToBackpack on trigger, tool destroyed on success, 15 s claim lifetime otherwise).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause Console does nothing By design: Studio only Client warns "skin has no Hotbar frame" / UI empty Skin prefab missing from the place (a rojo build has none) ITEM_NOT_IN_TOOLS_FOLDER No template with that exact name in ServerStorage.Tools BACKPACK_DISABLED BackpackEnabled was turned off (storage is on by default) Items won't merge into existing stacks CanStack is false by default; also check StackBlacklist, StackRequiredFields, and that merges happen via add or swap with StackOnSwap (never move/split) add x 5 gives one x5 stack Normal: CanStack blocks merges, not stack size. MaxStackSize caps the new stack. Set MaxStackSize = 1 for separate x1 items. OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS Another op holds the per-player lock (3 s timeout) [QuickNet] unknown event id N, dropping calls A call raced registration; the FullSync backstop heals it UUID commands (remove, drop, split, equip) fail with ITEM_NOT_FOUND UUIDs contain dots; quote the whole UUID (copy the quoted form from inv) or use a slot command New-solver type noise on Value/Computed Add explicit :: Fusion.Value<T> / :: Fusion.Computed<T>

Next: Glossary.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
After this page you know what the server enforces, what canon leaves open, and what to close before shipping.

The server owns the truth. The client predicts and converges.

docs.title: What the server enforces
docs.text:
• Every request goes through the same route as server code, under a per-player lock.
  • CoreStore validates slots, amounts, capacity, and stacking.
  • Drop honors Droppable; templates must exist in ServerStorage.Tools.
  • The debug console exists only in Studio (no remotes, role, or commands in a live server).

docs.title: What canon leaves open (decide before shipping)
docs.text:
Client-supplied items and metadata

The client-facing AddItem, AddToBackpack, AddToHotbar, and UpdateMetadata events forward input / updates to the routes with no key policy. A modified client can mint any template tool with any metadata, or rewrite metadata on its own items. Remove those listeners, or enforce a server-side allowlist/denylist before you rely on any metadata-driven rule.

  • Failure corrections (a FullSync behind every failed op) are not rate limited; only RequestInventorySync has the 15 s per-player throttle.
  • Nothing persists. State lives for the session (see Persistence).

docs.title: Ship checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Console confirmed Studio-only
  • [ ] Client Add*/UpdateMetadata removed or policy-gated
  • [ ] Debug prints/warns removed
  • [ ] Tools folder and skin prefabs present in the published place
  • [ ] Persistence hooked up, if your game needs it

docs.title: Wire Reference
docs.text: QuickNet events (StowayRemotes), one named table per event. Client ops run silent; the server talks back on failures and on server-initiated changes.

docs.title: Server → client
docs.text: Event When Payload InventoryAdded Replicated add uuid, slotType, slot, full item (server UUID wins) InventoryUpdated Stack absorb uuid, newAmount InventoryRemoved Remove / drop uuid, slotType?, slot? InventoryEquipped / InventoryUnequipped Equip changes uuid?, previousUUID? InventoryFullSync Swap/move/split/metadata/sort pushes, every failure, join, sync requests Items, Hotbar, Storage, equipped, weight, full settings snapshot InventoryRevert Failed swap/stack only success=false, fromSlot (log-only on receipt) LayoutChanged Skin/layout switch layout, skin SettingsChanged Sparse engine-setting change Patch (all fields optional)

docs.title: Client → server
docs.text: One FireServer per op: AddItem / AddToBackpack (input, options?), AddToHotbar (input, preferredSlot?), RemoveItem, SwapSlots / SwapStack / Move (from, to), Split, EquipSlot, UnequipSlot (bare), UpdateMetadata (uuid, updates), Sort (bare), Drop, plus bare RequestInventorySync.

docs.title: Replicate matrix
docs.text: Origin replicate Client hears Client op, accepted false Nothing (it already predicted) Client op, rejected false InventoryRevert (swap only) + FullSync Console / game code true Delta for add/remove/equip, FullSync otherwise

docs.title: Throttle
docs.text: Only RequestInventorySync is throttled: 15 s per player, stamped on every push so a boot request racing the join push coalesces. Failure corrections are not rate-limited.

docs.title: CoreStore API
docs.text: Pure Luau, no Roblox types. Every mutation returns a Result ({ok:true,value} / {ok:false,error={kind,message}}); error kinds: PermissionDenied, InvalidArgument, NotFound, NotAvailable. Auto-sort (Storage only) triggers after every mutating call when Sorting is on.

docs.title: Shapes
docs.text:
Everything below is built from four shapes:

SlotRef = { Type: "Hotbar" | "Storage", Slot: number }
-- `from` / `to`: the two ends of a swap, move, or drag.
-- `dest`: where a split-off stack lands (explicit slot, else auto-placed).

ItemInput = { Id: string?, Amount: number?, Metadata: ItemMetadata? }
-- `input`: what to add. Amount falls back through input.Amount, then
-- metadata.Amount, then metadata.StackAmount, then 1 (strings coerced,
-- garbage falls through, both keys cleaned out after).

AddOptions = { Placement: ("Auto" | "Hotbar" | "Backpack" | "Slot")?, Slot: number?, SlotRef: SlotRef? }
-- `opts`: where adds may land. `addToBackpack` forces Backpack,
-- `addToHotbar` forces Hotbar (+ optional slot number), `addToSlot` takes
-- an exact SlotRef that must be empty.

SettingsOverrides = { HotbarType?, MaxHotbarSlots?, Limit?, ... }
-- `overrides` on `new()`: every engine setting, all optional, merged over
-- defaults. Anything omitted keeps the default (see Settings).

docs.title: Create & inspect
docs.text: Function One line new(overrides?) Empty state; overrides merge over defaults getDefaultSettings() Cloned defaults getItem(state, uuid) O(1) lookup find(state, query) By ItemId and/or metadata (indexed on Rarity/Type) filter(state, predicate) Full scan getAllItems(state) Everything getHotbarItemCount / getStorageItemCount Counts isEquipped / isFull / hasHotbarSpace Predicates compact(state) Pack Dynamic hotbar (no-op on Static) setHotbarType(state, t) Switch packing (auto-compacts to Dynamic)

docs.title: Mutate
docs.text: Function One line add(state, input, opts?) Normalize → stack into existing → new stacks; overflow on cap addToBackpack / addToHotbar(state, input, slot?) / addToSlot Placement-forced adds remove(state, uuid, amount?) Partial decrements; full destroys + clears slot removeBySlot(type, slot, amount?) UUID lookup → remove swap(from, to) Positional exchange; absorbs when StackOnSwap allows swapStack(from, to) Delegates to swap (single stacking truth) move(from, to) Positional only — never stacks split(uuid, amount, dest?) Source keeps UUID; capped at MaxStackSize; rollback on failure updateMetadata(uuid, updates) Merge keys, no re-stack; delete via CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE sort(state) Storage only (hotbar never sorted) equip(uuid) / unequip() Set/clear EquippedItemUUID, idempotent

docs.title: Stacking
docs.text:
canStack needs all five: CanStack on, same Id, room under MaxStackSize, neither rarity blacklisted (Legendary/Mythic/Special), all StackRequiredFields (Rarity, Type) equal. Only add (when CanStack is on) and swap/swapStack (when StackOnSwap is on) merge. CanStack does not limit a new stack's size: a single add still creates stacks up to MaxStackSize. Amount fallback chain: input.Amount → metadata.Amount → metadata.StackAmount → 1 (strings coerced, garbage falls through, keys cleaned, Droppable defaults from DefaultDroppable).

Deep rulebook lives in Deep Dives: swap/move/split/ sorting/metadata-update rules, invariants, and complexity targets.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
StowayServerV3_0_0/init.luau: Init(CoreStore) injects the engine, createPlayer / get / removePlayer manage per-player states, and 13 routes mutate through one locked route() (3s per-player lock, pcall inside, adapters dispatched after).

Route Notes AddItem / AddToBackpack / AddToHotbar Template must exist (ITEM_NOT_IN_TOOLS_FOLDER); template attributes merge under caller metadata RemoveItem Partial or full SwapSlots / SwapStack / Move / Split Thin engine pass-through EquipSlot Clears character Tools, clones template, stamps attributes, parents to Character UnequipSlot Clears character Tools UpdateMetadata Engine merge/delete Sort Engine sort Drop Honors Droppable; reuses the equipped tool or clones; touch-stripped, tagged world drop 5 studs ahead

replicate is opt-in everywhere: omitted means no echo.

docs.title: Replication
docs.text:
QuickNet events (StowayRemotes wire). Client ops run silent (replicate=false) — the client already rendered them. Failures correct via FullSync.

Direction Events Server → client deltas InventoryAdded (full item, server UUID wins), InventoryUpdated (amount), InventoryRemoved, InventoryEquipped / InventoryUnequipped Server → client wholesale InventoryFullSync (items + slots + equipped + weight + full settings backstop) for swap/move/split/metadata/sort and every failure Server → client revert InventoryRevert on failed swap/stack (log-only on receipt) Client → server One FireServer per op + bare RequestInventorySync (15s per-player throttle; every push stamps the cooldown so join races coalesce) Settings / layout Sparse SettingsChanged patch + LayoutChanged, both live-applied

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Templates live in ServerStorage.Tools; attributes become metadata defaults (Description, Image, Droppable, IsGamepass, Rarity, Type). Equipped clones carry UUID/Amount/Id/metadata attributes. Drops are tagged world Tools; StowayPickup watches the tag and prompts the pickup back into AddToBackpack.

docs.title: Example: Cooldowns
docs.text:
example/cooldowns — skill cooldowns built purely on item metadata, zero engine changes. Browse the branch.

Designers set Cooldown (seconds) + FireOnEquip (kind); the server stamps CooldownEnd and gates re-equips; the client veils cooling slots until it lifts.

flowchart TD
    A[Item metadata: Cooldown + FireOnEquip] --> B{Kind?}
    B -->|A: fire-on-equip| C[Equip stamps CooldownEnd]
    B -->|B: use-after-equip| D[Tool click stamps CooldownEnd]
    C --> E[CooldownEnd gates re-equip]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Client veils the slot until it lifts]

docs.title: How it works, step by step
docs.text:
Grant. cooldown-demo Pickaxe a 5 adds the tool with { Cooldown = 5, FireOnEquip = true }. Plain metadata on a plain item — the engine doesn't know or care.

Kind-A fire. Pressing the bind runs equipAndClearNew, which first asks the gate: cooling + has duration → deny with a CooldownDenied flash, no server call. Otherwise it equips, fires fireSkill (local veil starts, SkillFired pops visuals, _expectEcho marks the UUID), then auto-unequips — the cooldown, not the equip, is what blocks the next press. Meanwhile the server's EquipSlot route stamps CooldownEnd inline and replicates, so late joiners learn it from state.

Kind-B fire. Equipping arms a server-owned Tool.Activated connection (_activatedConns, disconnected on equip/unequip/leave). A world click runs OnToolActivated: wrong item, unarmed, or cooling → ignore; otherwise stamp the end, replicate, unarm. Plain tools are never touched.

Gates everywhere. Server EquipSlot returns ON_COOLDOWN while locked. Client binds and slot clicks on cooling UUIDs go silent-dead — the veil is the feedback.

The observer. Stamps from elsewhere (another client, a rejoin) arrive via FullSync. observeCooldownEnds diffs CooldownEnd against _lastSeenEnd: own kind-A stamps (marked _expectEcho) record without refiring; fresh ones anchor a local veil off true remaining — ends live in Workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), one epoch for every machine, so rejoins never over-veil.

The launder. CooldownEnd is a required stack field on this branch, so a cooling stack can't be washed by merging into a fresh one (swap-absorb falls back to positional). Both gates wipe expired ends via METADATA_DELETE, so spent stacks restack. Client writes to all three keys are stripped at the wire; only the server stamps.

docs.title: Why no engine changes
docs.text: Cooldown is payload + external timing. Operations and Slots never see it: stacking identity just compares one more field, gates live on routes, veils read a local clock. The engine treats the keys as inert metadata.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
cooldown-demo Pickaxe a 5, press the bind. Watch the veil count down; hammer the bind while cooling and feel the denies. Then cooldown-demo sword b 8, equip, click in the world.

Key files: Interactions/CooldownService.luau, the observer + gates in Controller/ClientController.luau, stamps + watchers in server init.luau, the key policy in Communications.luau, cooldown-demo in Debug/ConchCommands.luau.

docs.title: Example: Locked Slots
docs.text:
example/locked-slots — metadata-keyed hotbar slot unlocks through USE, not possession. Browse the branch.

A token carries UnlocksHotbarSlot = N; equipping it and clicking consumes one unit, flips slot N out of Settings.LockedHotbarSlots, and FullSync teaches the client permanently. Merely holding the token unlocks nothing.

flowchart TD
    A[Token metadata: UnlocksHotbarSlot = N] --> B[Equip token + click]
    B --> C{Slot N locked?}
    C -->|No| D[Nothing consumed]
    C -->|Yes| E[Consume 1 unit + flip the lock]
    E --> F[FullSync teaches the client]

docs.title: How it works, step by step
docs.text:
The rule. Shared/Stoway/SlotLocks.luau is pure Luau both sides share: UNLOCK_FIELD = "UnlocksHotbarSlot", and isUnlocked(locked, slot) — a slot binds unless it's in the locked set. Locks live in Settings (default: slot 9), flipped server-side only. Nil set fails open.

The token. UnlocksHotbarSlot is authored as a Tool attribute (e.g. the PouchToken template); getDefaultMetadata copies it into item metadata untouched on every grant path, chat adds included.

The use. src/server/SlotUnlockExample.server.luau watches the UnlockToken tag. Clicking an equipped token runs one atomic tick: find the first inventory unit with a numeric UnlocksHotbarSlot, range-check it, no-op if already unlocked (nothing consumed), else RemoveItem one unit, flip the slot out of the locked set, SendFullSync. route() is synchronous, so rapid double-clicks see the flipped settings and no-op instead of double-consuming.

The guards. Server placement refuses locked slots; client Query.isHotbarSlotUnlocked gates binds, clicks, and the keybind badge (which captures the template color, never self-reads).

The way back. /relock re-locks slot 9, evacuating occupants to the nearest free hotbar slot (findNearestEmptyHotbarSlot). /locks prints per-slot verdicts, /meta prints token metadata.

docs.title: Why no engine changes
docs.text: Locks are a settings set plus two guards. No slot mechanic moves: unlock flips a boolean the engine already carries, and FullSync already teaches settings. The engine never learns what a lock is.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Chat commands on this branch: /addhot PouchToken, equip it, click → slot 9 unlocks. /locks to verify, /relock to lock it again.

docs.title: Example: New-Item Glow
docs.text:
example/new-item-glow — first-seen shine on one metadata flag, zero engine changes. Browse the branch.

IsNew is client-ephemera, never server truth: grants replicate it on (the client glows), the server strips it silently off (FullSync can never resurrect it). The NewGlow instance exists only while the flag is present. Equipping clears it locally, never sent back.

flowchart TD
    A[Add with IsNew, replicate on] --> B[Client glows the slot]
    A --> C[Server strips the flag silently]
    B --> D[Seen: equip clears it locally]
    C --> E[FullSync wipes stragglers]

docs.title: How it works, step by step
docs.text:
Grant. /addnew sword adds with { IsNew = true }, replicate on. The client renders the glow purely from metadata — on add, on sync, on metadata update. No bus, no signal, just the flag.

Strip. Right after granting, the server deletes the flag with CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE, replicate off — no echo, no event. Server state stays clean, so a later FullSync carries no IsNew and cleared glows stay cleared. Only brand-new stacks get the flag; pre-existing stacks keep whatever they had.

Seen. Equipping clears the flag through a client-side updateMetadata that is never sent back. Any FullSync wipes lingering glows anyway — implicit mark-all-seen.

Lifecycle. The NewGlow instance is created on flag, destroyed on clear. Slots without the flag carry no halo instances at all.

docs.title: Why no engine changes
docs.text: Glow is a render-only read of one key. The engine already merges, indexes, replicates, and deletes metadata — the feature is four calls composed in the right order with the right replicate flags.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Chat commands on this branch: /addnew sword — the new stack glows while the server copy is already clean. Equip it and watch the glow die locally.

docs.title: Client Events (Hooks/Signals) Specification
docs.text: Client-side UI event system for StowayClientV3. Any client system (notification service, sounds, shine, tutorials) can subscribe; skin HookFuncs modules are privileged subscribers, not the transport.

docs.title: Two-Layer Model
docs.text:
Generic payloads and skin-specific payloads are deliberately separate. There is no generic typed thing for skin differences.

  • Layer 1 — generic bus (Controller/ClientEvents.luau): fixed minimal payloads (slotType, index, uuid), typed once with SignalPlus, stable forever. External systems connect here.
  • Layer 2 — skin-direct calls: skin HookFuncs functions are invoked directly at call sites with skin-specific args (btn, frame, scope parts), annotated in the Studio module itself. Passing a button on one skin and nothing on another is expected.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Generic Bus Catalog
docs.text:
Signal Payload Fired from When SlotClicked (slotType: SlotType, index: number, uuid: string?) SlotView Activated tap/click lands (post drag-guard) SlotHovered (slotType, index) SlotView MouseEnter hover begins (frame/btn available via lookup, not payload) DragStarted (slotType, index) PointerDragService begin threshold crossed, ghost created DragEnded (slotType, index) PointerDragService end release, before commit Equipped (slotType, index) equip call sites res.ok only Unequipped (slotType, index) unequip call sites res.ok only ItemAdded (slotType, index) ClientController wrappers post-success (covers binds, drag, server deltas) ItemRemoved (slotType, index) ClientController wrappers post-success Swapped (fromType, fromSlot, toType, toSlot) ClientController wrappers post-success Selected (slotType, index) per-slot Observer on isEquipped any equip source (click, bind, server) Deselected (slotType, index) per-slot Observer on isEquipped any unequip source

SlotType is "Hotbar" | "Storage". Payloads never contain frames, buttons, or scopes — subscribers resolve visuals themselves.

docs.title: Layer 2 — Skin-Direct Calls
docs.text:
Skin functions keep their bespoke signatures. The contract lives IN the Studio modules (ReplicatedStorage.Stoway.GUI.<Skin>.HookFuncs, one per skin, self-contained --!strict, no requires — deliberately no backwards dependency into PlayerScripts). Reference shape:

OnSlotClick(slotType: SlotType, index: number, uuid: string?)
OnSlotHover(btn: GuiButton, slotType: SlotType, slotIndex: number)
OnDragStart(slotType, index) / OnDragEnd(slotType, index)
OnEquip(slotType, index) / OnUnequip(slotType, index)
OnItemAdd(slotType, index) / OnItemRemove(slotType, index)
OnSwap(slotType, index)
OnSelect(frame: Frame, slotType, slotIndex) / OnDeselect(frame, slotType, slotIndex)

DefaultHooks and MetalHooks may differ freely. Call sites invoke through untyped handles (SkinHandle.Hooks is { [string]: any }), so a call-site/hook mismatch is a runtime pcall warn, never a type error — the Studio annotations only check within the module.

Drag highlighting is a skin concern, not a bus contract: OnDragStart arms on the pressed slot only. A skin that wants to mark the swap destination tracks OnSlotHover itself — Persona keeps a held button and moves a hot outline with Fx:SetHot, then drops it in OnDragEnd. Hooks therefore may hold light per-gesture state; it must clear on OnDragEnd so a cancelled drag leaves nothing lit.

A code-built skin ships the table in the repo instead of a prefab folder: Skins/Persona returns its hooks on the handle (SkinHandle.Hooks) from Persona/Hooks.luau, which requires the shared CoreStore.Types and its own Fx runtime. Same call sites, same discipline — the table is still invoked through ClientEvents.CallHook.

docs.title: Type-Change Protocol
docs.text:
Sending something new (or nothing where something was sent) touches exactly two places, in order:

  1. Skin hook function — add/change the parameter in the signature.
  2. Fire site(s) — pass (or stop passing) the variable where the event fires.

Then playtest once: the pcall warn names the hook that drifted. Generic bus payloads (Layer 1) change only by full-team decision; they are stability-locked once external subscribers exist.

docs.title: Handler Discipline
docs.text:
• Bus fires are synchronous. External handlers stay fast; defer heavy work with task.defer.
  • Skin-direct calls go through ClientEvents.CallHook, which task.spawns every invocation before pcall-wrapping it. Spawn is mandatory: stock OnSlotHover yields (two task.waits in its tween) and a synchronous call would stall the input/drag thread. A throwing hook warns once with its name and never breaks inventory.
  • Connections parent to the layout scope. LayoutManager:Teardown cleans them — same discipline as the input/pointer leak sweeps.
  • Passed frames/buttons are borrowed, not owned. Subscribers must never destroy, reparent, or permanently restyle them (OnSelect's highlight stroke must be removed by OnDeselect).
  • Skin functions may assume only what the skin contract guarantees: a hovered slotbutton carries a UIStroke child (stock OnSlotHover tweens Thickness 0→5→0); OnSelect parents a SelectionHighlight UIStroke to the cell, OnDeselect destroys it.
  • Operation events fire on res.ok only — subscribers never see phantom events. OnSwap reports the DESTINATION slot. Move/Split/SwapStack successes intentionally fire nothing (no signal/hook exists for them).

docs.title: Worked Example — Notification Service
docs.text:
ClientEvents.ItemAdded:Connect(function(slotType, index)
    task.defer(function()
        SoundService:Play("ItemGet")
        ToastBus:Show(("New item in %s #%d"):format(slotType, index))
    end)
end)

The New-item white glow reads Metadata.IsNew, not the bus: glow while the flag is present, equip deletes the key via updateMetadata + METADATA_DELETE.

docs.title: CoreStore Specification
docs.text:
This document defines the exact behavior of every CoreStore operation as currently implemented. It is the source of truth for what the code does today.

New operations (swap, move, split, sort, updateMetadata) are defined in their own rule documents.

docs.title: InventoryState Shape
docs.text:
export type InventoryState = {
    -- O(1): UUID -> Item
    Items: { [string]: Item },

    -- O(1) to get all stack UUIDs for an item id
    -- ItemId -> array of UUIDs
    ItemsByID: { [string]: { string } },

    -- Slot -> UUID (Static: nil holes allowed)
    Hotbar: { string? },

    -- Array of UUIDs (Dynamic: packed, no holes)
    Storage: { string },

    -- O(1): UUID -> where this item currently lives
    LocationByUUID: { [string]: SlotRef },

    -- O(1): MetadataIndex[fieldName][fieldValue] -> array of UUIDs
    -- Indexed fields: Rarity, Type
    MetadataIndex: { [string]: { [string]: { string } } },

    EquippedItemUUID: string?,
    Weight: number,

    Settings: Settings,
}

docs.title: Field Rules
docs.text: Field Type Constraint Items { [string]: Item } Every key is a UUID. Every value is a valid Item. ItemsByID { [string]: { string } } Every key is an ItemId. Every value is an array of UUIDs that exist in Items. Hotbar { string? } Indexed from 1 to MaxHotbarSlots. Values are UUIDs or nil. Static mode preserves holes. Dynamic mode is packed. Storage { string } Contiguous array of UUIDs. No nil holes. Indices shift on remove. LocationByUUID { [string]: SlotRef } Every key is a UUID that exists in Items. Value matches actual placement. MetadataIndex { [string]: { [string]: { string } } } Two-level index. First key is field name (e.g. "Rarity"). Second key is stringified field value (e.g. "Legendary"). Value is array of UUIDs with that metadata. Indexed fields: Rarity, Type. Updated on create, destroy, and metadata change. EquippedItemUUID string? UUID of equipped item or nil. Must reference an existing item or be nil. Weight number Sum of Amount across all items in Items. Always >= 0.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Type Default Description HotbarType "Static" \| "Dynamic" "Static" Static keeps fixed slots (holes allowed); Dynamic packs and compacts. MaxHotbarSlots number 10 Number of hotbar slots (1..N). Limit number 15 Total Amount capacity. 0 = infinite. CanStack boolean true Allow merging into existing stacks. New stacks are still capped by MaxStackSize. MaxStackSize number 5 Max Amount per stack. Caps new stacks and splits; existing stacks are not re-split. BackpackEnabled boolean true Allow Storage. false rejects storage operations. StackOnSwap boolean false Allow swap/swapStack to merge. Requires CanStack = true; move never merges. Sorting boolean false Auto-sort Storage after mutations. Hotbar is never sorted. SortOrder "None" \| "Name" \| "Rarity" \| "ItemType" "None" Sort key when Sorting is on. Rarity is descending. StackRequiredFields { string } { "Rarity", "Type" } Metadata fields that must match to merge. StackBlacklist { [string]: boolean } { Legendary = true, Mythic = true, Special = true } Rarity values that never merge into existing stacks. DefaultDroppable boolean true Droppable default for new items that omit it. DebugLogs boolean true System print/warn logging.

These are engine fallbacks. Shared/Stoway/Settings.luau overrides them for players (Dynamic, merging off, backpack on, Default skin on StandardHotbarStorage).

docs.title: Add Operation
docs.text: API: CoreStore.add(state, itemData, options?)

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Normalize item data
   - Read Id (exact key)
   - Read Amount, or metadata.Amount, or metadata.StackAmount
   - Parse string amounts to number
   - Remove Amount and StackAmount from metadata
   - Apply Droppable from Settings.DefaultDroppable if not set
   - Default amount = 1

2. Validate
   - ItemId must be a non-empty string
   - Amount must be a positive number

3. Check capacity
   - If Limit > 0 and remaining capacity <= 0: return FULL
   - Cap total amount to remaining capacity (partial fill)

4. Attempt merging into existing stacks (only if CanStack = true)
   - Pass Placement to tryStack for placement-aware stacking
   - Reduce amountLeft by stacked amount
   - Track updatedItems (UUID -> new Amount)

5. Place remaining amount as new stacks (always runs)
   - Split into multiple stacks if amountLeft > MaxStackSize
   - Each new stack is capped at MaxStackSize
   - Placement priority based on options.Placement:

     Auto:    Hotbar -> Storage
     Backpack: Storage only
     Hotbar:  Hotbar only (optional slot number)
     Slot:    Specific SlotRef (must be empty)

   - If no space for next stack: stop, overflow = remaining amount

6. Return result
   - addedAmount = total amount successfully placed
   - overflow = amount that could not be placed (no space)

CanStack only gates step 4. Step 5 always runs, so a new stack can still reach MaxStackSize when merging is off.

docs.title: Overflow Example
docs.text:
Add Apple x12, MaxStackSize = 5, 5 slots available in Storage

Stack 1: Apple x5 -> Storage[1]
Stack 2: Apple x5 -> Storage[2]
Stack 3: Apple x2 -> Storage[3]  (remainder)

addedAmount = 12, overflow = 0

Add Apple x12, MaxStackSize = 5, 8 slots available total

Stack 1: Apple x5 -> Hotbar[1]
Stack 2: Apple x5 -> Hotbar[2]
Stack 3: Apple x2 -> Hotbar[3]

addedAmount = 12, overflow = 0

Add Apple x12, MaxStackSize = 5, Capacity = 10

Stack 1: Apple x5 -> placed
Stack 2: Apple x5 -> placed
No room for remainder

addedAmount = 10, overflow = 2

docs.title: Placement Modes
docs.text: Mode Behavior Auto (default) Try empty hotbar slot first. If hotbar full, try storage. Backpack Storage only. Bypasses hotbar entirely. Hotbar Hotbar only. Fails if no hotbar space. Optional Slot for specific slot. Slot Specific SlotRef placement. (Planned, not yet implemented)

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text:
Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Add succeeds with Ok({ addedItems, updatedItems, addedAmount, overflow }) — per-stack placements, per-UUID new amounts, total placed, and the amount that could not be placed. 

### Side Effects

- Creates Item entries in Items
- Updates ItemsByID
- Sets LocationByUUID for each new stack
- Increments Weight
- Appends to Storage or sets Hotbar slot

---

## Remove Operation

**API:** `CoreStore.remove(state, uuid, amount?)`

### Flow
1. Find item by UUID - If not found: return ITEM_NOT_FOUND

  1. Determine amount to remove
  2. Default: remove entire stack

  3. Cap to item.Amount (cannot remove more than exists)

  4. Partial removal (amount < item.Amount)

  5. Reduce item.Amount
  6. Decrement Weight

  7. Return remaining amount

  8. Full removal (amount >= item.Amount) a. Clear EquippedItemUUID if this item is equipped b. Decrement Weight by item.Amount c. Remove from Items d. Remove from ItemsByID (cleanup empty arrays) e. Remove from LocationByUUID f. Clear Hotbar slot or remove from Storage g. If HotbarType = "Dynamic": compact hotbar 

    ### Result Shape

Every mutation returns a `Result`: `{ ok = true, value = … }` or
`{ ok = false, error = { kind, message } }`. Remove succeeds with `Ok({
removedItem, remaining, slotType, slot })` — a copy of the removed data,
the amount left after a partial remove, and where it lived.

docs.title: Side Effects
docs.text:
• Decrements Weight
  • Removes Item from Items
  • Removes UUID from ItemsByID
  • Removes LocationByUUID entry
  • Clears Hotbar slot or shifts Storage
  • Compacts Hotbar if Dynamic

docs.title: Stack Rules
docs.text: Module: Stack.luau

docs.title: canStack Conditions
docs.text:
All conditions must be true for stacking:

1. Settings.CanStack = true
2. existingItem.Id == incomingItemId
3. existingItem.Amount < Settings.MaxStackSize
4. existingItem.Metadata.Rarity NOT in Settings.StackBlacklist
5. incomingMetadata.Rarity NOT in Settings.StackBlacklist
6. Metadata.matchesRequiredFields passes for all Settings.StackRequiredFields

docs.title: tryStack Flow
docs.text:
1. Look up ItemsByID[itemId] for candidate UUIDs
2. For each candidate (in order):
   a. If Placement is specified and not "Auto":
      - Backpack: only stack into items in Storage
      - Hotbar: only stack into items in Hotbar
   b. Check canStack conditions
   c. Calculate room = MaxStackSize - existingItem.Amount
   d. Transfer min(room, amount) into existing stack
   e. Increment Weight by transfer amount
   f. Reduce amount by transfer
3. Return total stacked amount and updated items map

docs.title: Placement-Aware Stacking
docs.text:
Stacking respects the Placement parameter:

Placement Stacking Target Auto or nil Any existing stack of the same item Backpack Only stacks in Storage Hotbar Only stacks in Hotbar

This ensures addToBackpack does not accidentally stack onto hotbar items.

docs.title: getItem(state, uuid)
docs.text:
• Complexity: O(1)
  • Returns: Item or nil
  • Behavior: Direct lookup in Items[uuid]

docs.title: findById(state, itemId)
docs.text:
• Complexity: O(k) where k = number of stacks with this ItemId
  • Returns: Array of Items
  • Behavior: Reads ItemsByID[itemId], then looks up each UUID in Items

docs.title: find(state, query)
docs.text:
• String query: Delegates to findById. O(k).
  • Table query with single indexed metadata field: Uses MetadataIndex for O(k) lookup where k = items matching that field value.
  • Table query with multiple indexed metadata fields: Picks the smallest MetadataIndex bucket, then filters remaining fields. O(k) where k = smallest bucket size.
  • Table query with no indexed metadata fields: Falls back to full Items scan. O(n).
  • Returns: Array of Items matching all query fields

docs.title: filter(state, predicate)
docs.text:
• Complexity: O(n) where n = total items
  • Returns: Array of Items where predicate returns true

docs.title: getAllItems(state)
docs.text:
• Complexity: O(n) where n = total items
  • Returns: Array of all Items

docs.title: Hotbar (Static Mode)
docs.text:
• Fixed size: 1 to MaxHotbarSlots
  • Nil holes allowed (slot 3 can be empty while slot 4 is filled)
  • setHotbarSlot(state, slot, uuid) - sets slot and updates LocationByUUID
  • clearHotbarSlot(state, slot) - sets slot to nil, removes LocationByUUID
  • findEmptyHotbarSlot(state) - returns first nil slot, or nil
  • compactHotbar(state) - no-op in Static mode

docs.title: Hotbar (Dynamic Mode)
docs.text:
• Same fixed size
  • No nil holes allowed — always packed left
  • The only available slot is the append position (first nil after the packed portion)
  • Operations that target a non-append slot are rejected with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE
  • compactHotbar(state) - shifts all items left to fill holes
  • Updates LocationByUUID for each shifted item
  • Only runs if HotbarType = "Dynamic"

docs.title: Dynamic Hotbar Slot Availability
docs.text:
In Dynamic mode, the hotbar is always [item1, item2, ..., itemN, nil, nil, ...]. The only "available" slot is findEmptyHotbarSlot(state) — the first nil after the packed portion.

Use CoreStore.setHotbarType(state, "Dynamic") to switch types — it auto-compacts the hotbar. Alternatively, call CoreStore.compact(state) after manually changing Settings.HotbarType.

Operation Dynamic Mode Behavior add (no preferred slot) Appends to end via findEmptyHotbarSlot add (preferred slot) Preferred slot is ignored; always appends to end swap Hotbar→Hotbar, dest occupied Allowed (reorder within packed portion) swap Hotbar→Hotbar, dest empty Rejected: DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE move Hotbar→Hotbar Rejected: DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE (no empty slots in packed portion) move Storage→Hotbar Allowed only if toRef.Slot == findEmptyHotbarSlot() split to Hotbar Allowed only if destination.Slot == findEmptyHotbarSlot()

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Dynamic array, no holes
  • appendStorage(state, uuid) - appends to end, updates LocationByUUID
  • removeStorageAt(state, index) - removes and shifts all subsequent items left
  • Updates LocationByUUID for each shifted item

docs.title: LocationByUUID
docs.text:
• Always reflects actual placement
  • Updated whenever an item moves between slots
  • Entry created on item placement
  • Entry removed on item destruction
  • Entry updated on hotbar compaction

docs.title: Compaction
docs.text: Compaction is the process of packing a Dynamic hotbar's items left to eliminate nil holes. It only applies when HotbarType = "Dynamic". In Static mode, compaction is a no-op.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
compactHotbar(state):
  1. If HotbarType ~= "Dynamic": return false (no-op)

  2. Create empty array packedHotbar
  3. writeIndex = 1

  4. For readIndex = 1 to MaxHotbarSlots:
     a. uuid = Hotbar[readIndex]
     b. If uuid exists:
        - packedHotbar[writeIndex] = uuid
        - If readIndex ~= writeIndex:
            Mark changed = true
            Update LocationByUUID[uuid].Slot = writeIndex
        - writeIndex += 1
     c. If uuid is nil: skip (hole eliminated)

  5. If changed: state.Hotbar = packedHotbar
  6. Return changed

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Before (holes at slots 2, 4):
  Slot:  [1]  [2]  [3]  [4]  [5]
         "A"  nil  "B"  nil  "C"

After compaction:
  Slot:  [1]  [2]  [3]  [4]  [5]
         "A"  "B"  "C"  nil  nil

LocationByUUID updated:
  "A" -> Slot 1 (unchanged)
  "B" -> Slot 2 (was Slot 3)
  "C" -> Slot 3 (was Slot 5)

docs.title: When Compaction Runs
docs.text: Operation Compacts? Notes remove() Yes After clearing hotbar slot move() hotbar→storage Yes After setting hotbar slot to nil swap() hotbar→empty storage Yes After clearing hotbar slot

docs.title: Static vs Dynamic Behavior
docs.text: Behavior Static Dynamic Holes after remove Preserved (nil stays) Eliminated (items shift left) Slot indices after remove Unchanged All items after the hole shift down by 1 Client visibility All MaxHotbarSlots frames always visible Empty frames hidden, visible ones reindexed Full state sync needed No Yes (when compaction changes indices)
