docs.text:
• h = MaxHotbarSlots (hotbar size)
  • s = #state.Storage (storage item count)
  • n = total items across both containers
  • k = matching items for a given ItemId or metadata value
  • f = number of fields (StackRequiredFields for canStack, indexed fields for MetadataIndex, keys in updates for updateMetadata)

docs.title: CoreStore Invariants
docs.text:
These are the structural guarantees that CoreStore maintains at all times. Every operation must preserve these invariants. Future operations must be designed to maintain them.

Violations of these invariants indicate a bug.

docs.title: INV-1: UUID Ownership
docs.text:
Every UUID present in Hotbar or Storage must exist as a key in Items.

forall uuid in Hotbar[u]: Items[uuid] ~= nil
forall uuid in Storage[i]: Items[uuid] ~= nil

docs.title: INV-2: Single Location
docs.text:
Every Item exists in exactly one location. No UUID appears in both Hotbar and Storage simultaneously.

forall uuid in Items:
    (exists i: Hotbar[i] == uuid) XOR (exists j: Storage[j] == uuid)

docs.title: INV-3: LocationByUUID Accuracy
docs.text:
Every entry in LocationByUUID must match the item's actual placement. If an item is in Hotbar slot 3, LocationByUUID[uuid] must be { Type = "Hotbar", Slot = 3 }.

forall uuid in Items:
    LocationByUUID[uuid].Type == "Hotbar" implies Hotbar[LocationByUUID[uuid].Slot] == uuid
    LocationByUUID[uuid].Type == "Storage" implies Storage[LocationByUUID[uuid].Slot] == uuid

docs.title: INV-4: ItemsByID Consistency
docs.text:
Every UUID in ItemsByID[itemId] must reference an existing item with that Id. No stale UUIDs.

forall itemId, forall uuid in ItemsByID[itemId]:
    Items[uuid] ~= nil
    Items[uuid].Id == itemId

docs.title: INV-5: ItemsByID Completeness
docs.text:
Every Item in Items must have its UUID present in ItemsByID[item.Id].

forall uuid in Items:
    uuid in ItemsByID[Items[uuid].Id]

docs.title: INV-6: Weight Accuracy
docs.text:
Weight equals the sum of Amount across all items in Items.

state.Weight == sum(Items[uuid].Amount for all uuid in Items)

docs.title: INV-7: Weight Non-Negative
docs.text:
Weight is always >= 0.

state.Weight >= 0

docs.title: INV-8: Hotbar Bounds
docs.text:
Hotbar indices are in the range [1, MaxHotbarSlots].

forall i in Hotbar:
    1 <= i <= MaxHotbarSlots

docs.title: INV-9: Storage Contiguity
docs.text:
Storage has no nil holes. Indices are contiguous from 1 to #Storage.

forall i in [1, #Storage]:
    Storage[i] ~= nil

docs.title: INV-10: Hotbar Static Holes
docs.text:
In Static mode, Hotbar may contain nil values. In Dynamic mode, Hotbar has no nil holes after compaction. The only available slot in Dynamic mode is the append position.

HotbarType == "Dynamic" implies:
    forall i in [1, writeIndex-1]: Hotbar[i] ~= nil
    findEmptyHotbarSlot(state) == writeIndex  (the append position)

docs.title: INV-11: Equipped Validity
docs.text:
EquippedItemUUID either references an existing item in Items or is nil.

state.EquippedItemUUID == nil or Items[state.EquippedItemUUID] ~= nil

docs.title: INV-12: Settings Change Through Defined Paths
docs.text: Settings start from construction-time overrides but do change during a state's lifetime: setHotbarType, sparse SettingsChanged pushes, and the debug console toggles all mutate them. What never happens is silent drift — every change flows through one of those paths and replicates.

docs.title: INV-13: MaxStackSize Positive
docs.text:
MaxStackSize must be >= 1.

Settings.MaxStackSize >= 1

docs.title: INV-14: Limit Non-Negative
docs.text:
Limit must be >= 0. Limit = 0 means infinite.

Settings.Limit >= 0

docs.title: INV-15: Add Preserves Existing Items
docs.text: Adding items never modifies existing items except through stacking (increasing Amount).

docs.title: INV-16: Remove Preserves Other Items
docs.text: Removing an item never modifies any other item in the inventory.

docs.title: INV-17: Partial Remove Preserves UUID
docs.text: A partial remove (amount < item.Amount) keeps the same UUID. Only the Amount changes.

docs.title: INV-18: MaxStackSize Enforcement
docs.text:
No item's Amount may exceed MaxStackSize after any operation. This is enforced unconditionally — regardless of CanStack or StackOnSwap settings.

forall uuid in Items:
    Items[uuid].Amount <= Settings.MaxStackSize

Why this matters: MaxStackSize is a structural constant that defines what a valid stack looks like. If stacks can exceed it, canStack returns false for them (Amount >= MaxStackSize), making them invisible to stacking logic. This creates zombie stacks that can never receive more items. The cap is always enforced in createItem and split.

docs.title: INV-19: MetadataIndex Consistency
docs.text:
Every Item in Items with indexed fields (Rarity, Type) must have a corresponding entry in MetadataIndex. Conversely, every entry in MetadataIndex must reference an existing Item in Items.

forall uuid in Items:
    if Items[uuid].Metadata.Rarity ~= nil:
        uuid in MetadataIndex["Rarity"][tostring(Items[uuid].Metadata.Rarity)]
    if Items[uuid].Metadata.Type ~= nil:
        uuid in MetadataIndex["Type"][tostring(Items[uuid].Metadata.Type)]

forall field in MetadataIndex:
    forall value in MetadataIndex[field]:
        forall uuid in MetadataIndex[field][value]:
            Items[uuid] ~= nil

docs.title: Trigger Matrix
docs.text:
Operations that modify state and which invariants they must preserve:

Operation Modifies Items Modifies Hotbar Modifies Storage Modifies Weight Modifies MetadataIndex Must Preserve add Yes (create) Yes (set slot) Yes (append) Yes (+) Yes (add) ALL remove Yes (reduce/destroy) Yes (clear) Yes (remove) Yes (-) Yes (remove) ALL swap No (unless StackOnSwap absorbs) Yes (exchange) Yes (exchange) No Conditional (absorb destroys) INV-1,2,3,4,5,8,9,19 swapStack No (unless StackOnSwap absorbs) Yes (exchange) Yes (exchange) No Conditional (absorb destroys) INV-1,2,3,4,5,8,9,19 move No Yes (set/clear) Yes (append/remove) No No INV-1,2,3,4,5,8,9,19 split Yes (create) Yes (set slot) Yes (append) Yes (+) Yes (add) ALL sort No No Yes (reorder) No No INV-1,2,3,4,5,9,19 updateMetadata Yes (modify) No No No Yes (update) ALL

The INV list above is the contract. There is no verifyInvariants checker in the repo — operations preserve these by construction.

docs.title: Metadata Update Rules
docs.text: Metadata updates allow external systems to modify item metadata after creation. All metadata is mutable in CoreStore.

docs.title: API
docs.text: CoreStore.updateMetadata(state, uuid, updates) -> MetadataUpdateResult

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description state InventoryState The inventory state uuid string UUID of the item to update updates { [string]: any } Key-value pairs to merge into metadata

docs.title: Deleting a Field
docs.text:
Lua tables can never hold a nil value, so { Enchant = nil } produces an empty table and deletes nothing. To remove a metadata field, set it to the METADATA_DELETE sentinel:

CoreStore.updateMetadata(state, uuid, { Enchant = CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE })

CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE is "__STOWAY_DELETE__", a namespaced string exported from the CoreStore facade and from ReplicatedStorage/Shared/Stoway/StowayRemotes.luau. It survives the wire as a plain string, so clients delete fields with StowayRemotes.METADATA_DELETE. Deleting an indexed field (Rarity/Type) also evicts the UUID from its MetadataIndex bucket.

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text: Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Update succeeds with Ok({ updatedFields }) — the list of fields that changed. Metadata changes never re-stack or split anything.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Validate
   - UUID must exist in Items

2. Apply updates
   - For each key in updates:
     - If key exists: overwrite value
     - If key does not exist: add key-value pair
     - If value is the `METADATA_DELETE` sentinel: remove key from metadata
       (note: `{ Key = nil }` is an empty table in Lua and deletes nothing)

3. Return result

docs.title: Mutability Rules
docs.text: All metadata is mutable. This includes fields that affect stacking behavior.

docs.title: Mutable Fields (Examples)
docs.text: Field Effect of Change Rarity May affect stack blacklist eligibility Type May affect stack required fields matching Description No stacking impact Damage No stacking impact Durability No stacking impact Droppable No stacking impact (used by drop system) Image No stacking impact Custom fields No stacking impact (unless added to StackRequiredFields)

docs.title: Stacking Impact
docs.text: When metadata changes, CoreStore must decide what happens to existing stacks.

docs.title: Scenario 1: Metadata Change Does Not Affect Stacking
docs.text:
If the changed fields are not in StackRequiredFields and not in StackBlacklist, no stacking changes occur.

Example: Update Damage from 10 to 20
Result: Item unchanged in stacking. No re-stack needed.

docs.title: Scenario 2: Metadata Change Breaks Stacking
docs.text:
If the item was part of a stack and the metadata change makes it no longer stackable with its siblings, the item is not automatically un-stacked. The stack remains as-is until a future operation (like split or remove) separates it.

Example: Item has Rarity = "Common", stacked with other Commons
         Update Rarity to "Legendary" (blacklisted)
Result: Stack remains. But next time items are added, this stack
        will not accept new Legendary items from other stacks.
        CanStack check will reject new merges into this stack.

Reason: Automatically un-stacking would create cascading side effects. The caller should explicitly split if they want separation.

docs.title: Scenario 3: Metadata Change Enables Stacking
docs.text:
If the item was not stackable and now is, nothing happens immediately. Future add operations may stack into this item.

Example: Item has Rarity = "Legendary" (blacklisted)
         Update Rarity to "Common"
Result: Stack remains. Next add of Common items may stack into this one.

docs.title: Stacking Re-evaluation (Future)
docs.text:
A future reStack(state, uuid) function could be added to explicitly re-evaluate an item's stacking position:

-- Future API
CoreStore.reStack(state, uuid)
  - Remove item from current stack position
  - Re-run stacking logic to find best stack
  - If no compatible stack found, create standalone

This is not yet implemented. For now, metadata updates do not trigger automatic re-stacking.

docs.title: Index Updates
docs.text:
Metadata changes do not affect: - Items (the Item object is modified in-place) - ItemsByID (UUID stays the same, Id stays the same) - LocationByUUID (position stays the same) - Hotbar/Storage (slot stays the same) - Weight (Amount is unchanged)

Only the Item.Metadata table is modified.

docs.title: Sorting Interaction
docs.text: If Settings.Sorting = true, auto-sort runs after metadata update. This may reorder items if the metadata change affects sort order (e.g., changing Rarity changes rarity-based sort position).

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text: Scenario Behavior updates is empty No change, return Ok with empty updatedFields Key set to CoreStore.METADATA_DELETE Remove key from metadata (and from MetadataIndex if indexed) Key set to nil (inline) No-op — { Key = nil } produces an empty table, key untouched Key set to same value No change, but listed in updatedFields Update equipped item Allowed, no equip/unequip triggered Update blacklisted item to un-blacklisted No immediate re-stack

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
• Validation: O(1)
  • Apply updates: O(k) where k = number of fields updated
  • Stacking evaluation: O(1) (check against settings)
  • Sorting trigger: O(n log n) if Sorting enabled
  • Total (no sort): O(k)
  • Total (with sort): O(n log n)

docs.title: Item Metadata on the Wire — Open-Ended Schema
docs.text: How item metadata is transmitted between client and server over QuickNet, and how it changed from a strict (closed) schema to an open dynamic dict.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
• Metadata is always { [string]: any } at the storage layer (see CoreStore/Types.luau — ItemMetadata).
  • On the wire it is sent as an open dynamic dict { [string]: any }.
  • Any consumer-defined custom field (tool attributes, stats, rarity, etc.) transmits automatically — no schema edits needed ever.
  • On the client, read metadata values by convention, not by runtime type-checking.
  • Only ReplicatedStorage/Shared/Stoway/StowayRemotes.luau (the wire) is open. CoreStore storage logic is untouched.

docs.title: The problem (the old/naive way)
docs.text:
QuickNet schemas are generally enumerative: you list the fields and their types. A strict metadata schema looks like:

local ItemMetadata = {
    Description = data.optional(data.String),
    Image = data.optional(data.String),
    IsGamepass = data.optional(data.Boolean),
    Rarity = data.optional(data.String),
    Droppable = data.optional(data.Boolean),
    Type = data.optional(data.String),
}

This serializes a fixed set of fields into fixed buffer offsets. Any key not in the schema has no type-code, so QuickNet silently does not send it. Because items may carry arbitrary custom metadata (e.g. FireDmg, Enchant, Skill, or anything read from a tool's attributes), the strict form forced a new line in the schema every time you added a custom field:

local ItemMetadata2 = {
    -- ...the six built-ins...
    FireDmg = data.optional(data.NumberU16),   -- hand-declared
    Enchant = data.optional(data.String),      -- hand-declared
}

This is brittle and annoying — exactly the friction a [string]: any metadata contract was trying to avoid.

docs.title: The fix (how we do it now)
docs.text:
QuickNet supports dynamic dicts that carry their own type-tag per value (Serialize.luau — getDataType, encodeAny, encodeDict). We use that so metadata stays fully open on the wire:

-- StowayRemotes.luau — ONE definition covers every metadata payload.
local MetadataSchema = { [data.String]: data.any }

The six built-in fields remain a documented reference only — they are a naming convention, not enforced wire fields:

--   Description (string)   Image (string)     IsGamepass (boolean)
--   Rarity (string)        Droppable (bool)   Type (string)

docs.title: Before vs. after
docs.text: Old (strict) New (open, current) Declare custom fields Required — one per field Never Unlisted key behavior Silently dropped on the wire Transmitted intact Value typing on receive Strong, per-field any (per-value tag preserved) Wire cost Fixed offsets, fast paths Type-tag byte per value (slightly larger/slower) Schema shape dictStatic dict / Any

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A world-drop tool carries attributes Rarity, Damage, FireDmg, Skill. The server reads them on pickup and grants server-side — clients never mint items (see the trust model):

-- StowayPickup (server): attributes in, AddToBackpack with replicate on
Stoway.AddToBackpack(player, {
    Id = "MagicSword",
    Metadata = attrs,   -- Rarity, Damage, FireDmg, Skill all transmitted
}, nil, true)

The server replicates it back via InventoryAdded, with every metadata key intact:

Remotes.InventoryAdded:FireClient(player, {
    uuid = added.uuid,
    slotType = added.slotType,
    slot = added.slot,
    item = { UUID = item.UUID, Id = item.Id, Amount = item.Amount, Metadata = item.Metadata },
})

Because each value carries its own type-tag byte, FireDmg = 25 arrives as a number and Skill = "Flaming" as a string — types survive the round-trip.

docs.title: Deleting a field
docs.text:
Lua tables cannot hold a nil value, so { Enchant = nil } is an empty table and deletes nothing. Setting a metadata key to the "__STOWAY_DELETE__" sentinel removes it on the server.

StowayRemotes.UpdateMetadata:FireServer({
    uuid = uuid,
    updates = { Enchant = StowayRemotes.METADATA_DELETE },
})
-- Server: CoreStore.updateMetadata(state, uuid, { Enchant = METADATA_DELETE })
-- -> item.Metadata.Enchant == nil

The sentinel is a namespaced string, so it serializes through QuickNet's data.any payload with no wire-schema changes. Both sides reference the same constant from StowayRemotes.luau.

docs.title: Client-side guidelines (no runtime checks)
docs.text:
On the client, metadata arrives as any. Follow these conventions instead of running runtime type-checks:

local meta = item.Metadata

local fireDmg  = meta.FireDmg   -- any: a number when present
local rarity   = meta.Rarity    -- any: one of the Rarity strings
local enchant  = meta.Enchant   -- any: a string
  • Use if v == nil to test presence, not type(v).
  • Trust the naming convention: Rarity is a string, Droppable a boolean, Type a string — code against that assumption.
  • If you need a specific type guarantee, if type(v) == "number" then ... end is the only place a check belongs (e.g., before math), but do not sprinkle checks over every read.
  • Custom fields are yours to name and document for your own game; there is no enforced registry on the wire.

docs.title: Querying custom metadata (server-side reference)
docs.text:
Open metadata does not change how CoreStore indexes it:

  • Only Rarity and Type are reverse-indexed into MetadataIndex (O(1) bucket lookups) via INDEXED_METADATA_FIELDS in CoreStore/Operations.luau.
  • Custom fields are not indexed by default. Query via a predicate:
local fiery = CoreStore.filter(state, function(item)
    return (item.Metadata.Enchant or "") == "Fire"
end)
  • Custom fields are stored verbatim in Item.Metadata; they are not dropped unless they collide with the reserved keys Amount / StackAmount (which CoreStore consumes as the stack amount).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Layer Changed? Shared/Stoway/StowayRemotes.luau (wire schema) Yes — open dict CoreStore/Types.luau (ItemMetadata) No — already [string]: any CoreStore storage / communication adapter No Data persistence surfaces No

docs.title: Move Rules
docs.text: Move transfers an item from one slot to another. It is a purely positional operation. Move never triggers stacking.

docs.title: API
docs.text: CoreStore.move(state, fromRef, toRef) -> MoveResult

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description state InventoryState The inventory state fromRef SlotRef Source slot toRef SlotRef Destination slot (must be empty)

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text: Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Move succeeds with Ok({ hotbarCompacted: boolean? }).

docs.title: Core Rule
docs.text:
Move is swap where the destination is empty. Move is purely positional. Move never triggers stacking.

If the destination is occupied, the operation fails. If you want to stack, use add (for new items) or swap with StackOnSwap = true (for existing items).

docs.title: Why Move Does Not Stack
docs.text:
Consider: Apple x3 in Storage, Apple x2 in Hotbar[1], Hotbar[2] is empty.

CanStack = true, StackOnSwap = false

Move Storage[1] -> Hotbar[2]:
  Apple x3 moves to Hotbar[2]
  Hotbar[1] still has Apple x2
  Result: Two separate stacks, no merging

Swap Storage[1] -> Hotbar[1] (with StackOnSwap = true):
  Apple x3 absorbs into Apple x2 (up to MaxStackSize)
  Result: Stacked

Stacking during move would create implicit behavior. If you want to stack, the caller must explicitly use swap with StackOnSwap = true.

docs.title: Hotbar -> Hotbar (empty slot)
docs.text:
Move item from one hotbar slot to another empty hotbar slot.

Static mode: Holes are allowed. The destination can be any empty slot.

fromUUID = Hotbar[fromSlot]

Hotbar[fromSlot] = nil
Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID

Dynamic mode: The hotbar is always packed. There are no empty slots within the packed portion. Any move to an empty slot is rejected with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE because the destination does not exist in the packed array.

if HotbarType == "Dynamic":
    return Err("DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE")  -- NotAvailable

docs.title: Hotbar -> Storage (append)
docs.text:
Move item from hotbar to storage. Hotbar slot becomes nil (Static) or triggers compaction (Dynamic).

fromUUID = Hotbar[fromSlot]

Hotbar[fromSlot] = nil
table.insert(Storage, fromUUID)

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID
hotbarCompacted = compactHotbar(state)

docs.title: Storage -> Hotbar (empty slot)
docs.text:
Move item from storage to an empty hotbar slot. Storage shifts left.

Static mode: The destination can be any empty hotbar slot.

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]

Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID
table.remove(Storage, fromSlot)

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID
Update LocationByUUID for all shifted storage items

Dynamic mode: The destination must be the append position (the first nil slot after the packed portion). If toRef.Slot != findEmptyHotbarSlot(state), the operation is rejected with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE.

if HotbarType == "Dynamic":
    appendSlot = findEmptyHotbarSlot(state)
    if toRef.Slot != appendSlot:
        return Err("DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE")  -- NotAvailable

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]

Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID
table.remove(Storage, fromSlot)

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID
Update LocationByUUID for all shifted storage items

docs.title: Storage -> Storage (reorder)
docs.text:
Move item within storage to a different index.

Validate toRef.Slot bounds: 1 <= toRef.Slot <= #Storage + 1

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]

table.remove(Storage, fromSlot)
table.insert(Storage, toSlot, fromUUID)

Update LocationByUUID for all affected storage items

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. fromRef must contain an item
2. toRef must be empty
3. BackpackEnabled check (if destination is Storage)
4. Hotbar bounds check (if either slot is Hotbar)
5. Storage destination bounds:
   If toRef.Type == "Storage": toRef.Slot must be in [1, #Storage + 1]
   (Append is allowed for empty destination)

docs.title: Equipped Item Behavior
docs.text: EquippedItemUUID follows the UUID. Moving an equipped item from Hotbar[1] to Storage does not unequip it.

docs.title: Sorting Interaction
docs.text: If Settings.Sorting = true, auto-sort runs after the move completes.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
• Hotbar -> Hotbar: O(1)
  • Hotbar -> Storage: O(1) append + O(h) compaction
  • Storage -> Hotbar: O(n) for storage shift
  • Storage -> Storage: O(n) for storage shift

docs.title: Settings Sync
docs.text: How per-player engine settings (MaxHotbarSlots, HotbarType, Sorting, …) travel server → client, and when to send what.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. One remote, sparse payloads. SettingsChanged carries ONLY the fields that changed (all-optional schema). Each mutation site fires its own literal, so intent is visible exactly where state changes. No remote zoo.
  2. Structural vs cosmetic. A stale structural field forks state (optimistic ops apply under the wrong rules with no rollback); a stale cosmetic field only misrenders until the next update:
Setting Kind If stale/dropped HotbarType, MaxHotbarSlots Structural Positional divergence (holes vs packed, phantom slots) CanStack, MaxStackSize, StackOnSwap, StackRequiredFields, StackBlacklist Structural Stacking rules differ per side Limit, BackpackEnabled, DefaultDroppable Structural-lite Capacity/gating checks differ Sorting, SortOrder Cosmetic Display order only, no state fork
  1. Convergence backstop. FullSync carries the full settings snapshot, so a dropped partial heals on the next op-driven resync. Sparse sends give immediacy; the snapshot gives convergence. Never rely on partials alone.
  2. Single atomic apply. The client overlays present fields onto _state first, then one sync() fans out to atoms (SetEngineSettings). Later ops re-apply the same values instead of clobbering atoms with the boot snapshot. Unknown keys are ignored by construction.

docs.title: QuickNet findings (observed, not theorized)
docs.text:
• All traffic multiplexes through shared remotes with numeric event ids. The client logs [QuickNet] unknown event id 7, dropping calls: calls whose id isn't recognized are dropped, not queued. Any protocol that assumes delivery (like sparse partials) needs a convergence story — rule 3.
  • Schemas are strict and stateful: table-nesting optional() wrappers mutate in place, so schema tables must be inline-fresh and registered exactly once (the single-use rule). Bare-enum optionals are safe to share.
  • The wire is one static dict per event (FireServer(a, b) misaligns — proven live). Every payload is one named table.
  • Serialization erases type nominals: schema types and domain types share shapes but not identities, hence the single any seam at the boundary with explicit annotations at call sites.

docs.title: If you use regular remotes instead
docs.text: With plain RemoteEvents (reliable, ordered, schemaless), drops are not a factor — so the backstop matters less and sparse singles are beneficial mainly for intent clarity: each mutation sends exactly what it changed, nothing is over-sent, and readers see the contract per call site. Keep the defensive habits anyway: typeof checks on receipt, unknown-key tolerance on apply, atomic apply-then-fanout.

docs.title: Sorting Rules
docs.text: Sorting reorders items within containers based on configurable criteria. In CoreStore, sorting applies to Storage only. The Hotbar is never sorted — it is always user-controlled.

docs.title: API
docs.text: CoreStore.sort(state) -> SortResult

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text: Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Sort succeeds with Ok({ storageOrder? }) — the new storage UUID order, only when it changed.

docs.title: Trigger Model
docs.text: Sorting is automatic. It runs after any operation that mutates slot contents when Settings.Sorting = true.

docs.title: Operations That Trigger Sort
docs.text: Operation Triggers Sort Scope add (incl. addToBackpack, addToHotbar, addToSlot) Yes Storage only remove (incl. removeBySlot) Yes Storage (reorder remaining) swap (incl. swapStack) Yes Storage (if affected) move Yes Storage (if affected) split Yes Storage (if destination) updateMetadata Yes Storage (reorder on criteria change) sort No (already sorting) N/A

docs.title: Trigger Timing
docs.text:
Sort runs after the primary operation completes and all invariants are satisfied. It is the last step in any mutating operation.

1. Execute primary operation (add, remove, swap, etc.)
2. If Settings.Sorting = true: run sort
3. Return result

docs.title: Storage Only
docs.text:
Sorting only affects Storage. The Hotbar is never sorted — it is always user-controlled.

Slots.sortHotbar() exists as a utility function for callers who need it, but Operations.sort() and triggerAutoSort() only sort Storage.

docs.title: Sort Criteria
docs.text: Determined by Settings.SortOrder:

docs.title: SortOrder = "Name"
docs.text:
Sort by item.Id alphabetically.

"Apple" < "Potion" < "Sword"

docs.title: SortOrder = "Rarity"
docs.text:
Sort by item.Metadata.Rarity using a fixed rarity rank. Items are sorted descending (highest rarity first):

Special = 7 (first)
Mythic = 6
Legendary = 5
Epic = 4
Rare = 3
Uncommon = 2
Common = 1 (last)

Unknown rarities sort after all known rarities (equivalent to rank 99).

Ties compare the rarity string itself, so equal rarities keep whatever order table.sort leaves them in — not guaranteed stable, not alphabetical by id.

docs.title: SortOrder = "ItemType"
docs.text:
Sort by item.Metadata.Type alphabetically.

"Ammo" < "Consumable" < "Food" < "Weapon"

docs.title: SortOrder = "None"
docs.text: No sorting. Default behavior.

docs.title: Sort Stability
docs.text: Sort runs on table.sort, which is not stable: equal keys may come out in any order. Don't rely on insertion order surviving a sort.

docs.title: Sort Algorithm
docs.text:
1. Read current item order from Storage
2. Sort items by SortOrder criteria
3. Write new UUID order back to Storage
4. Update LocationByUUID for all moved items

docs.title: Storage Sort
docs.text:
sortedUUIDs = tableSort(Storage, by SortOrder)
Storage = sortedUUIDs
Update LocationByUUID for each UUID at new index

docs.title: Invariants Preserved
docs.text:
Sorting preserves all state invariants:

  • INV-1 (UUID Ownership): No items created or destroyed
  • INV-2 (Single Location): Only reorders within container
  • INV-3 (LocationByUUID): Updated for all moved items
  • INV-4,5 (ItemsByID): Not affected (no item changes)
  • INV-6 (Weight): Not affected (no amount changes)
  • INV-9 (Storage Contiguity): Reorder maintains contiguity

docs.title: Manual Sort
docs.text: In the future, CoreStore.sort(state, { Order = "Rarity" }) may accept options to override Settings for a one-time sort. This is not yet implemented.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
• Reading items: O(n)
  • Sorting: O(n log n)
  • Writing back: O(n)
  • LocationByUUID updates: O(n)
  • Total: O(n log n) where n = number of items in Storage

docs.title: Split Rules
docs.text: Split divides an existing stack into two stacks. The source stack keeps a reduced amount, and a new stack is created with the split amount.

docs.title: API
docs.text: CoreStore.split(state, uuid, amount, destination?) -> SplitResult

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description state InventoryState The inventory state uuid string UUID of the stack to split amount number Amount to move to the new stack destination SlotRef? Optional specific destination slot

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text:
Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Split succeeds with Ok({ sourceUUID, newUUID, sourceAmount, newAmount, newSlotType, newSlot, hotbarCompacted? }) — the source keeps its UUID, the new stack gets a fresh one. 

---

## Validation
1. UUID must exist in Items 2. Amount must be positive 3. Amount must be < item.Amount (cannot split entire stack; use remove instead) 4. If destination specified: a. Destination slot must exist b. Destination slot must be empty c. BackpackEnabled check if destination is Storage 
---

## Flow
1. Validate split request - amount >= 1 - amount < sourceItem.Amount

  1. Cap split amount
  2. splitAmount = min(amount, MaxStackSize)
  3. This is unconditional: always enforced regardless of CanStack

  4. Excess stays in source (e.g., split 8 with MaxStackSize=5 → splitAmount=5, source keeps 3)

  5. Reduce source stack

  6. sourceItem.Amount -= splitAmount

  7. State.removeWeight(state, splitAmount)

  8. Create new stack

  9. Generate new UUID

  10. Create Item with:

    • UUID = new UUID
    • Id = sourceItem.Id
    • Amount = splitAmount (capped at MaxStackSize)
    • Metadata = deep copy of sourceItem.Metadata

  11. Place new stack

  12. If destination specified: place in that slot

  13. If no destination: follow placement chain (Auto -> Hotbar -> Storage)

  14. Update indexes

  15. Add new UUID to Items
  16. Add new UUID to ItemsByID[itemId]
  17. Add new UUID to MetadataIndex (indexed fields: Rarity, Type)
  18. Set LocationByUUID for new UUID

  19. Increment Weight by splitAmount

  20. Return result 

    ---

## Placement Chain (No Destination Specified)

When no destination is provided, the new stack follows the standard placement chain:

  21. Try empty hotbar slot (first available)
  22. If hotbar full and backpack enabled, append to storage

  23. If hotbar full and backpack disabled, fail with NO_SPACE 

    Split never changes total weight (source loses what the new stack gains),
so `Limit` is never consulted — `NO_SPACE` only means nowhere to put the
new stack.

### With Specific Destination

When a destination SlotRef is provided:
    If destination.Type == "Hotbar": Validate slot bounds and emptiness

    If HotbarType == "Dynamic": appendSlot = findEmptyHotbarSlot(state) if destination.Slot != appendSlot: fail with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE

    Set Hotbar[destination.Slot] = newUUID

If destination.Type == "Storage": Validate BackpackEnabled Validate destination.Slot bounds: 1 <= destination.Slot <= #Storage (the append position #Storage + 1 is INVALID_STORAGE_SLOT) Insert at destination.Slot in Storage Shift subsequent items if needed 

---

## Stacking Interaction

Split does NOT attempt to stack the new stack into existing stacks at the destination. The new stack always goes to the next available slot via the placement chain.
If you want to stack after split: 1. Split creates two separate stacks 2. Use swap with StackOnSwap = true to merge them ```

This is consistent with the rule: stacking during slot operations only happens via add (when CanStack = true) or swap with StackOnSwap = true.

docs.title: Equipped Item Behavior
docs.text: Split does not affect equipped state. The source UUID remains the same, so if it was equipped, it stays equipped with the reduced amount.

docs.title: Sorting Interaction
docs.text: If Settings.Sorting = true, auto-sort runs after the split completes. This may move the new stack within Storage.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text: Scenario Behavior amount == 0 Fail: INVALID_AMOUNT amount >= item.Amount Fail: CANNOT_SPLIT_FULL (use remove instead) Split into max stack New stack capped at MaxStackSize, excess stays in source. Always enforced, even if CanStack = false. Split 8 from 10, MaxStackSize = 5 splitAmount = min(8, 5) = 5. Source keeps 5, new stack gets 5. Source has amount = 2, split 1 Source becomes 1, new stack has 1 No hotbar space and backpack disabled Fail: NO_SPACE Splitting equipped item Allowed, source keeps UUID and equipped state

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
• Validation: O(1)
  • Source reduction: O(1)
  • New stack creation: O(1)
  • Placement (auto): O(1) hotbar + O(1) storage append
  • Placement (stacking): O(k) where k = candidate stacks
  • Storage insert at position: O(n) for shift

docs.title: Swap Rules
docs.text:
Swap exchanges the positions of two items in the inventory. It is a positional operation that does not create or destroy items.

Stacking during slot operations: Swap is the only slot operation that can trigger stacking (via StackOnSwap). Move and split never stack. Note: add operations attempt to merge into existing stacks when CanStack = true — new stacks still cap at MaxStackSize.

docs.title: API
docs.text: CoreStore.swap(state, fromRef, toRef) -> SwapResult

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description state InventoryState The inventory state fromRef SlotRef Source slot: { Type = "Hotbar" \| "Storage", Slot = number } toRef SlotRef Destination slot: { Type = "Hotbar" \| "Storage", Slot = number }

docs.title: Result Shape
docs.text: Every mutation returns a Result: { ok = true, value = … } or { ok = false, error = { kind, message } }. Swap succeeds with Ok({ hotbarCompacted: boolean? }) — true when a Dynamic hotbar was compacted along the way.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Before any swap executes, these checks run:

1. BackpackEnabled check:
   If BackpackEnabled = false and either slot is Storage: return BACKPACK_DISABLED

2. Hotbar bounds check:
   If fromRef.Type == "Hotbar": slot must be in [1, MaxHotbarSlots]
   If toRef.Type == "Hotbar": slot must be in [1, MaxHotbarSlots]

3. Storage source existence:
   If fromRef.Type == "Storage": Storage[fromRef.Slot] must exist
   (Swapping FROM an empty storage slot is invalid)

4. Storage destination bounds:
   If toRef.Type == "Storage": toRef.Slot must be in [1, #Storage + 1]
   (Append is allowed for empty destination)

docs.title: Hotbar <-> Hotbar
docs.text:
Both slots are in the hotbar. Simple exchange.

Static mode: Both slots are valid. Holes are allowed.

fromUUID = Hotbar[fromSlot]
toUUID = Hotbar[toSlot]

Hotbar[fromSlot] = toUUID
Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID

Update LocationByUUID for both UUIDs

Dynamic mode: Only occupied slots are valid. The destination must contain an item (reorder). If the destination is nil (empty), the operation is rejected with DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE. Dynamic hotbar is always packed — no holes exist, so swapping with an empty slot is meaningless.

if HotbarType == "Dynamic" and toUUID == nil:
    return Err("DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE")  -- NotAvailable

docs.title: Storage <-> Storage
docs.text:
Both slots are in storage. Reorder within the array.

Validate toRef.Slot bounds: 1 <= toRef.Slot <= #Storage + 1

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]
toUUID = Storage[toSlot]

Storage[fromSlot] = toUUID
Storage[toSlot] = fromUUID

Update LocationByUUID for both UUIDs

docs.title: Hotbar -> Storage (destination occupied)
docs.text:
Move hotbar item into storage, storage item into hotbar.

fromUUID = Hotbar[fromSlot]
toUUID = Storage[toSlot]

Hotbar[fromSlot] = toUUID
Storage[toSlot] = fromUUID

Update LocationByUUID for both UUIDs

docs.title: Hotbar -> Storage (destination empty)
docs.text:
Move hotbar item to storage. Hotbar slot becomes nil (Static) or triggers compaction (Dynamic).

fromUUID = Hotbar[fromSlot]

Hotbar[fromSlot] = nil
table.insert(Storage, fromUUID)

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID
hotbarCompacted = compactHotbar(state)

docs.title: Storage -> Hotbar (destination occupied)
docs.text:
Move storage item into hotbar, hotbar item into storage.

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]
toUUID = Hotbar[toSlot]

Storage[fromSlot] = toUUID
Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID

Update LocationByUUID for both UUIDs

docs.title: Storage -> Hotbar (destination empty)
docs.text:
Move storage item to hotbar. Storage shifts left.

fromUUID = Storage[fromSlot]

Hotbar[toSlot] = fromUUID
table.remove(Storage, fromSlot)

Update LocationByUUID for fromUUID
Update LocationByUUID for all shifted storage items

docs.title: StackOnSwap Behavior
docs.text:
Setting: Settings.StackOnSwap (system-level, not per-player)

When StackOnSwap = true AND CanStack = true:

Before executing the positional swap, CoreStore checks if the items can stack. If they can, the source item is absorbed into the destination stack instead of swapping positions.

If StackOnSwap AND CanStack:
    fromItem = Items[fromUUID]
    toItem = Items[toUUID]

    if toItem exists AND canStack(fromItem, toItem):
        -- Absorb source into destination
        room = MaxStackSize - toItem.Amount
        transfer = min(fromItem.Amount, room)

        toItem.Amount += transfer
        fromItem.Amount -= transfer

        if fromItem.Amount <= 0:
            -- Source destroyed, remove from all indexes
            remove(fromUUID)

        -- No positional swap happens
        return Ok({})

When StackOnSwap = false (default) OR CanStack = false:

Swap is purely positional. Items exchange slots regardless of whether they could stack.

docs.title: SwapStack Behavior
docs.text: CoreStore.swapStack(state, fromRef, toRef) is the explicit drag-and-drop stack route. It uses the same directional source-to-target absorption as swap, and it respects both Settings.StackOnSwap and Settings.CanStack. When either setting is off, or the items cannot stack, it falls back to the ordinary positional swap behavior.

docs.title: Equipped Item Behavior
docs.text:
EquippedItemUUID follows the UUID, not the slot. If the equipped item is swapped from slot A to slot B, EquippedItemUUID still points to the same UUID. No equip/unequip logic needed.

-- Before swap
state.EquippedItemUUID = "uuid_sword"
-- sword is in Hotbar[1]

-- After swap (Hotbar[1] <-> Storage[1])
state.EquippedItemUUID = "uuid_sword"
-- sword is now in Storage[1]

docs.title: Sorting Interaction
docs.text: If Settings.Sorting = true, auto-sort runs after the swap completes. This may reorder Storage.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
• Hotbar <-> Hotbar: O(1)
  • Storage <-> Storage: O(1) (direct UUID swap)
  • Cross-container (occupied dest): O(1) for direct swap
  • Cross-container (empty dest): O(h) compaction for Hotbar -> Storage; O(n) for Storage -> Hotbar (shift)
  • With StackOnSwap + canStack: O(k) where k = candidate stacks
